column1: # CURRENT STATE NOTE (RACE-2659-1, #2852, 2026-10-05) — read before the review text below.
# The "13 genuine races" the review block reports is its ORIGINAL count, not the current
# state. 11 remain UNSAFE-OPEN. #2657 ((*KeyorixCore).TransitionMembership) and #2659
# ((*KeyorixCore).inviteMemberWithMode) were closed by #2669 and are relabelled STALE here:
# both now run their state change and their grant/removal side effect under
# WithNamedLock(membershipLockKey(project, user)) (INV-CORE-44), so the guard no longer
# flags either function. That staleness was verified the way this file's STALE class
# prescribes — by deleting each row and confirming
# TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck stays green — not by inspection.
# DEDUPED (2026-10-09): this file used to hold 188 data rows for only 31 distinct keys
# (roughly six copies of every row, accumulated by repeated appends from every PR that
# touched it), with 16 of those 31 keys carrying two DIFFERENT versions of themselves —
# one copy already superseded by a later fix but never removed. Collapsed to exactly 31
# rows, one per key. For each of the 16 contested keys, the surviving version was picked
# by reading the CURRENT production code (and, where one exists, its cross-replica
# Postgres regression test) directly, not by date or by trusting either row's own claim —
# three of the sixteen had conflicting or self-contradicting review history (e.g.
# (*KeyorixCore).AddSecretDependency's two versions directly dispute whether the #2660 fix
# is cross-replica-safe; TestCTAReview_AddSecretDependency_CrossReplicaCycle_Postgres,
# unskipped and asserting the fix holds, settled it). Re-verified
# TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck stays green after the dedup, and that it
# still fails when a fragment-vs-flat-file duplicate is planted (readLedgerRows,
# ledger_fragments_test.go, is unaffected by this — it already treated a legacy-only
# duplicate as non-fatal and a fragment duplicate as fatal; this PR does not touch that
# logic). This did NOT run scripts/ledgers/migrate-to-fragments.sh — rows stay in this flat
# file, migration to per-key fragments is still the coordinator's call. New rows go in
# docs/check-then-act-lock-exempt.d/, not here.
# GUARD-2 Item 4: reviewed exemptions for TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck
# (internal/core/guards/check_then_act_lock_guard_test.go). Every hit from this guard's first run
# (31) was read against the real code and classified below. The first classification said
# none was a genuine cross-replica race; the independent second review (see the review
# column and the block below) found 13 that are. See
# https://github.com/keyorixhq/keyorix/issues/2564 for the per-class writeup.
# Columns: function <TAB> class <TAB> reason <TAB> review
# Independent second review (C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW, #2564, 2026-10-03): every row was
# re-read against the code on main (callees down to the SQL issued) and its "safe" claim
# tested against a concrete two-replica Postgres interleaving. The review column records
# the verdict: CONFIRMED (class and reason accurate), RECLASSIFIED (conclusion holds, class
# and/or reason rewritten), or UNSAFE (a real cross-replica check-then-act gap: class set to
# UNSAFE-OPEN, reason names the tracking issue and the skipped Postgres race test in
# internal/core/concurrency_check_then_act_exempt_review_postgres_test.go that reproduces
# it). UNSAFE-OPEN rows stay in this file — removing them would turn the guard red without
# fixing anything — until the fixing PR un-skips its test and drops/relabels the row.
# Classes added by the review:
#   SERIAL-EQUIV  the check reads state another actor can change concurrently, but every
#                 interleaving's end state equals some serial order of the two operations.
#   STALE         no longer a guard hit on main (checked by removing the row: the guard
#                 stays green); kept because review does not delete rows. NOTE: the guard
#                 does not detect stale rows, so these do not fail anything.
#   UNSAFE-OPEN   a confirmed open race; see the issue in the reason.
#   PARENT-LOCKED was UNSAFE-OPEN: a child row (share, ACL grant, lease, environment, config)
#                 could commit under a concurrently deleted parent. Now closed in storage:
#                 the child write and a FOR SHARE re-read of the live parent run in one
#                 transaction, which rolls back if the parent is gone (lockLiveParent,
#                 INV-STORE-21). The guard sees only WithNamedLock, not a row lock, so the
#                 row stays, with the reason naming the conditional write and its test.
(*KeyorixCore).ActivateMFA
column3: requireReauth re-proves the caller and is not invalidated by a concurrent writer. The state the activation depends on (which TOTP secret the code was validated against) is re-asserted by a conditional write: since #2655 ActivateMFASecret is UPDATE ... WHERE user_id = ? AND secret_enc = <validated ciphertext>, returning matched=false when a concurrent BeginMFAEnrollment swapped the secret, and ActivateMFA then fails closed (ErrMFAEnrollmentChanged) and rolls back the whole activation. Guard: TestCTAReview_ActivateMFA_vs_BeginMFAEnrollment_CrossReplicaPostgres, TestActivateMFA_SecretSwappedAfterValidation_FailsClosed.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=UNSAFE (was REAUTH-FRESHNESS); fixed=#2655 (conditional write, C-RACE-FIX-C)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).AddSecretDependency
column3: requireSecret (secret_dependencies.go) only checks existence; edges outlive soft-delete by design, so a racing DeleteSecret equals serial add-then-delete; the peer is authorized separately. The integrity-relevant check (the cycle check) is not this require* call but CreateSecretDependencyExclusive's own read, and since #2660 that read-check-insert runs under WithNamedLock(secretDependencyGraphLockKey(project)) inside LockedCreateSecretDependencyExclusive, which every edge-adding caller goes through, so two replicas can no longer both commit A->B and B->A (TestCTAReview_AddSecretDependency_CrossReplicaCycle_Postgres). The guard still flags this row because requireSecret precedes the locked helper.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=RECLASSIFIED (reason corrected: "atomic DB primitive" claim was false)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).ApproveSecretAccessRequest
column3: storage.UpdateAccessRequest is a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE state='pending' (returns ok bool), fails closed on a stale read; requireAdminAuthorityAt is an actor-authority check unrelated to the race; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).CreateDynamicSecretConfig
column3: #2651 closed: the post-insert DSN write is now SetDynamicSecretConfigAdminDSN, a targeted UPDATE of admin_dsn_enc/admin_dsn_meta/updated_at that cannot write disabled=false back over a concurrent DeleteProject (#369); and LocalStorage.CreateDynamicSecretConfig re-reads the project FOR SHARE after its insert, in one transaction, rolling back if it is gone (deleteProjectCascade locks the project first). requireDynamicSecretAdminAuthority remains an actor check. Proven: TestCTAReview_CreateDynamicSecretConfig_vs_DeleteProject_CrossReplicaPostgres (fails with the full-row Save), _DeleteProjectAfterInsert_ (fails without the insert re-check).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).CreateOIDCBinding
column3: requireAdminAuthorityAt is an actor-authority check, not shared mutable state; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).CreateUserWithAssignments
column3: The ceiling checks (users.go:336-416) and SoD set-check (:363) target a principal that does not exist until CreateUserWithRoleGrants (:365) commits it and its grants atomically, so no concurrent grant can address it; the flagged AddPasswordHistory (:378) is a best-effort history row. Residual: a concurrently created SoD policy can miss the new user — common to every grant path; see #2564.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=RECLASSIFIED (was AUTHZ-ACTOR; reason omitted the real write)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).DeleteSessionsForUserExcept
column3: requireUserCredentialsRevokeAuthority is an actor-authority check; the revoke write is idempotent and lock-free-safe per inventory item 16; see #2564.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=CONFIRMED (note: the requireUserCredentialsRevokeAuthority check is actor-only, so a stale pass equals revoke-then-demote; "inventory item 16" is about revocation honored on the next read, a different property; no live HTTP/gRPC caller since ADR-108)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).FinishWebAuthnRegistration
column3: requireReauth (webauthn.go:160) re-verifies credentials; its single-use inputs (TOTP step, step-up grant) and the ceremony itself (ConsumeWebAuthnSession, local_webauthn.go: WHERE used_at IS NULL) are conditional updates, and credential_id is unique-indexed, so stale reads are serial-equivalent; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).GrantSecretACL
column3: #2649 closed: LocalStorage.CreateOrUpdateSecretACL now runs its upsert and a FOR SHARE re-read of the live secret node in one transaction and rolls back if the node is gone; DeleteSecret UPDATEs (locks) the secret row before its CWE-284 ACL cascade, so the cascade either sees the committed grant or the grant fails closed. The IsProjectMember read remains serial-equivalent. Proven: TestCTAReview_GrantSecretACL_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres, TestCTAReview_GrantSecretACL_DeleteSecretAfterUpsert_CrossReplicaPostgres, TestLocalACL_RefusesSoftDeletedSecret.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).InviteGlobal
column3: No longer a guard hit on main: the require* checks moved into buildGlobalInvite (invitations.go:392-422), which writes nothing. Would be safe anyway: the write is a pending invitation granting nothing, and accept re-runs ceiling + SoD under sodGrantLockKey (invitations.go:497-515). Row kept per #2564 (rows are never deleted by review).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).InviteToProject
column3: No longer a guard hit on main: the require* check moved into buildProjectInvite (invitations.go:139), which writes nothing. Would be safe anyway: the write is a pending invitation granting nothing, and accept re-runs ceiling + SoD under sodGrantLockKey (invitations.go:497-515). Row kept per #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).IssueLease
column3: #2652 closed: LocalStorage.CreateDynamicSecretLease inserts an active lease and re-reads its config (still enabled) FOR SHARE in one transaction, rolling back with ErrDynamicSecretConfigDisabled if it was disabled; IssueLease then revokes the just-minted credential (cleanupOrphanedRole). DeleteProject's #369 cascade UPDATEs (locks) the config row and lists leases to revoke only after commit, so it either sees the lease or the lease fails closed. Proven: TestCTAReview_IssueLease_vs_DeleteProject_CrossReplicaPostgres, TestCTAReview_IssueLease_DeleteProjectAfterInsert_CrossReplicaPostgres, TestCreateDynamicSecretLease_ActiveRefusedOnDisabledConfig.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RejectSecretAccessRequest
column3: Delegates to RejectAccessRequest, whose write is a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE state='pending' (ok bool), fails closed on a stale read; requireAdminAuthorityAt is an actor-authority check; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RemoveSecretDependency
column3: requireSecret is an existence/accessibility check, not the race-relevant decision; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RemoveUserFromGroup
column3: Both guards and the write run inside withGroupProjectAdminGuardLocks (project_members.go:439), which holds lastAdminGuardLockKey PLUS every affected projectAdminGuardLockKey(P), sorted (#2352). Documented residual: the project set is computed before the per-project locks (project_members.go:431). The direct-removal path (#2658) now counts only live holders and takes the same lastAdminGuardLockKey (RemoveUserRole -> removeGlobalAdminRoleIfApplicable).
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=RECLASSIFIED (reason incomplete: named only the global key)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RenewLease
column3: A stale liveness pass cannot revive a credential: the cascade's RevokeLease drops it on the target, so the end credential state is serial-equivalent. Side note (LOW, bookkeeping): UpdateDynamicSecretLease is a stale full-row Save (local_dynamic.go:108) that can flip a concurrently revoked lease row back to active while the credential stays dead; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RestoreEnvironment
column3: #2656 closed: LocalStorage.RestoreEnvironment now un-deletes the environment and re-reads the project FOR SHARE in one transaction, rolling back if it is gone; deleteProjectCascade row-locks the project BEFORE sweeping environments, so the sweep either sees the restored environment or the restore fails closed. The core ceiling check (requireAuthorityToReinstateProjectRoles) remains serial-equivalent. Proven: TestCTAReview_RestoreEnvironment_vs_DeleteProject_CrossReplicaPostgres, _DeleteProjectAfterUpdate_, _InsideDeleteProjectCascade_ (the last one fails without the cascade's up-front lock).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RestoreGroup
column3: No longer a guard hit on main: GetGroupRoles, requireGlobalAdminToReinstateAdminRoles and tx.RestoreGroup all run inside WithNamedLock(sodGrantLockKey("group", id)) (groups.go:177-198, #2469). The original reason ("not shared mutable state") was wrong: the check reads the group's role set. Row kept per #2564.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=RECLASSIFIED (was AUTHZ-ACTOR; stale, now locked)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RestoreProject
column3: requireAuthorityToReinstateProjectRoles reads the project's grant set (contended state, not only the actor), but a grant racing in commits under its own grantor ceiling, so the outcome equals restore-then-grant; storage.RestoreProject is one idempotent transaction. Consider a lock anyway for consistency with RestoreGroup (#2469); see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RevokeAllPersonalAccessTokensForUser
column3: requireUserCredentialsRevokeAuthority is an actor-authority check; the revoke write is idempotent and lock-free-safe per inventory item 16; see #2564.
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=CONFIRMED (note: the requireUserCredentialsRevokeAuthority check is actor-only, so a stale pass equals revoke-then-demote; "inventory item 16" is about revocation honored on the next read, a different property; no live HTTP/gRPC caller since ADR-108)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RevokeUserSessions
column3: requireAdminRankCeilingForTarget reads target AND actor roles (not actor-only); a stale pass equals revoke-then-promote and only removes access; the write is an idempotent DELETE (local_auth.go:213). Inventory item 16 (revocation honored on next read) is a different property; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).SetSecretAutoRotate
column3: #2650 fixed: the write is UpdateSecretRotationConfig, a column-scoped conditional UPDATE of only auto_rotate/rotation_length/rotation_charset/rotation_backend/rotation_ref/updated_at WHERE id=? AND project_id=? AND rotation_backend=<pre-read value the admin gate was decided on> AND deleted_at IS NULL; matched=false fails closed. A concurrent DeleteSecret, MoveSecret or admin re-bind makes it match 0 rows, and ownership/other columns are never written. Proven: TestCTAReview_SetSecretAutoRotate_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres; structural: TestSetSecretAutoRotate_IsColumnScoped.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).ShareSecret
column3: #2646 closed: LocalStorage.CreateShareRecord now runs its upsert and a FOR SHARE re-read of the live secret in one transaction and rolls back if the secret is gone; DeleteSecret UPDATEs (locks) the secret row before its #370 share cascade, so every interleaving either fails the share or lets the cascade see it. Ownership side remains serial-equivalent. Proven: TestCTAReview_ShareSecret_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres, TestCTAReview_ShareSecret_DeleteSecretAfterInsert_CrossReplicaPostgres.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).ShareSecretWithGroup
column3: #2647 closed: same CreateShareRecord transaction as ShareSecret (#2646) — the group share rolls back if a racing DeleteSecret got there first. The recipient-group scope read remains serial-equivalent. Proven: TestCTAReview_ShareSecretWithGroup_vs_DeleteSecret_CrossReplicaPostgres.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).StartImpersonation
column3: requireEqualOrGreaterAdminAuthority reads target AND actor roles (not actor-only); a stale pass equals start-then-role-change, and ReauthorizeImpersonation re-checks the ceiling on every session validation (auth.go, 60s cache in authz.go), bounding the session exactly as in the serial case; see #2564.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).TransitionMembership
column3: #2657, CLOSED by #2669: the state CAS and its grant/removal side effect now run together under WithNamedLock(membershipLockKey(project, user)), the same key inviteMemberWithMode takes (INV-CORE-44). No longer a guard hit — the function holds a named lock, so the guard does not flag it; staleness verified the way this file's STALE class prescribes, by deleting the row and confirming TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck stays green. Proving tests: TestCTAReview_TransitionMembership_ActivateVsRevoke_CrossReplicaPostgres (un-skipped, passes -count=20), TestInvariant6_MembershipLockIsLoadBearing_Activate (re-fails with the lock mutated away).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).UpdateOwnProfile
column3: #2654 fixed: UpdateOwnProfile never sets IsActive, so UpdateUser takes its default branch, whose write is UpdateUserIfActiveStateMatches — now a column-scoped conditional UPDATE (username/email/display_name/is_active/updated_at only, WHERE id=? AND is_active=? AND deleted_at IS NULL, matched=false fails closed with ErrUserActiveStateConflict). It no longer writes password_hash/account_state/MFA/lockout columns, so a concurrent password change, suspension or MFA enable cannot be reverted. Proven: TestCTAReview_UpdateOwnProfile_vs_ChangePassword_CrossReplicaPostgres; structural: TestUserProfileWrites_AreColumnScoped.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).UpdateSharePermission
column3: #2648 fixed: UpdateShareRecord is now a column-scoped conditional UPDATE (permission/expires_at/updated_at only, WHERE id=? AND deleted_at IS NULL); against a concurrently revoked share it matches 0 rows and fails closed (ErrorShareNotFound) instead of Save's upsert resurrecting it. requireLiveOwnerAuthority is an actor-authority check (AUTHZ-ACTOR shape). Proven: TestCTAReview_UpdateSharePermission_vs_RevokeShare_CrossReplicaPostgres; structural: TestUpdateSharePermission_IsColumnScoped.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).UpdateUser
column3: #2653 fixed: the ceiling check (users.go) precedes every branch; every branch persists via UpdateUserIfActiveStateMatches, now a column-scoped conditional UPDATE (username/email/display_name/is_active/updated_at only, WHERE id=? AND is_active=? AND deleted_at IS NULL, matched=false fails closed with ErrUserActiveStateConflict), so a concurrent SetAccountState/SetPasswordHash/MFA/lockout write is never reverted. Last-admin is separately locked (lastAdminGuardLockKey). Proven: TestCTAReview_UpdateUser_vs_SuspendUser_CrossReplicaPostgres; structural: TestUserProfileWrites_AreColumnScoped.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).deleteGroupGuarded
column3: Both guards and the write run inside withGroupProjectAdminGuardLocks (project_members.go:439): lastAdminGuardLockKey PLUS every affected projectAdminGuardLockKey(P), sorted (#2352). Documented residual: the project set is computed before the per-project locks (project_members.go:431). The direct-removal path (#2658) now counts only live holders and takes the same lastAdminGuardLockKey (RemoveUserRole -> removeGlobalAdminRoleIfApplicable).
column4: reviewed_by=C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW; verdict=RECLASSIFIED (reason incomplete: named only the global key)

column1: (*KeyorixCore).inviteMemberWithMode
column3: #2659, CLOSED by #2669: the ceiling check, the `active` create and the role grant now all run under WithNamedLock(membershipLockKey(project, user)), the same key TransitionMembership takes, so a revoke can no longer land between the create and the grant (INV-CORE-44). The original reason's diagnosis was right (the only lock that applied was AssignUserRole's sodGrantLockKey("user"), inventory item 3, not item 10). No longer a guard hit — the function holds a named lock; staleness verified by deleting the row and confirming TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck stays green. Proving tests: TestCTAReview_InviteMemberOpenMode_vs_Revoke_CrossReplicaPostgres (un-skipped, passes -count=20), TestInvariant6_MembershipLockIsLoadBearing_OpenModeInvite (re-fails with the lock mutated away).
